monument: Arjuna's Penance / Descent of the Ganges
title: Descent of the Ganges (Mahabalipuram)
source_org: Sketchfab (independent creator, Jules Morel — Toulouse; self-described researcher)
license: Sketchfab Standard (all rights reserved / view-only) — no download button present
format: Sketchfab-hosted viewer only; no download offered
captured_by: Jules Morel (@jules.morel) — profile lists occupation 'Researcher specialized in Surface Reconstruction from 3D points', skills include Photogrammetry, 3D Reconstruction, Voxel; his other Sketchfab uploads are terrestrial-LiDAR forest plots and point-cloud surface reconstructions, strongly corroborating this is a genuine scan rather than a hand model
notes: THE MOST SIGNIFICANT FINDING OF THIS SEARCH. This is the only located 3D capture explicitly titled as the Descent of the Ganges / Arjuna's Penance relief itself, at 1.1M vertices — plausibly high enough resolution to carry the carved figures the project needs. Description text quotes Wikipedia's '96 by 43 feet (29 m x 13 m)' dimensions, matching this project's own 29.26 x 13.10 m plate almost exactly. HOWEVER: no license/download option is shown on the page (Standard/all-rights-reserved by default), the creator has no contact info beyond Sketchfab, and there is no description of capture method, coverage (full panel vs. a section), resolution adequacy, or permission status. This needs a direct message to the author (Sketchfab handle @jules.morel, personal site https://julesmorel.com/) requesting license terms or a paid/negotiated release — it is NOT currently usable without that outreach, but it is the single best lead found.

title: The Shore Temple, Mahabalipuram (Street View)
source_org: Google Arts & Culture (partner: Archaeological Survey of India)
license: Not stated on page; standard Google Arts & Culture terms (viewing only, not a 3D download)
format: Google Street View-style 360 degree panoramic photography — NOT a downloadable 3D mesh or point cloud
captured_by: Archaeological Survey of India (credited partner institution)
notes: IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: This is Google's older Street View-based Arts & Culture feature (panoramic photos users can pan around in), separate from Google/CyArk's 'Open Heritage' program which hosts true downloadable-viewer 3D laser scans. Do not confuse the two. There is no evidence this is 3D geometry at all — it behaves like indoor Street View. Same caveat applies to the sibling Google Arts & Culture pages for Olakkanesvara Temple, Krishna Mandapam, and The Seven Pidaris found in the same partner collection (all Street View panoramas, not 3D models).

title: Google Arts & Culture 'Open Heritage' project (CyArk/Google 3D laser-scan program) — Mahabalipuram NOT included
notes: NOTHING FOUND for any Mahabalipuram monument. Open Heritage covers 26 sites in 18 countries (e.g. Bagan, Chichen Itza, Rapa Nui, Temple of Apollo, Thomas Jefferson Memorial). Cross-checked against the full CyArk project list (cyark.org/projects/, fetched and enumerated ~140 project titles) — CyArk's only India projects are the Elephanta Caves (Mumbai) and the Gateway of India (Mumbai). Neither Mahabalipuram nor any of its 12 monuments appears anywhere in CyArk's public project catalog.

title: Zamani Project (zamaniproject.org) — Mahabalipuram NOT included
source_org: Zamani Project, University of Cape Town
notes: UNVERIFIED by direct site fetch — the site's 'explore sites' page did not render usable content via automated fetch/browser (JS-heavy, returned empty body twice). However Zamani's own public description (via Wikipedia and third-party coverage, cross-checked) states its scope is 'The African Cultural Heritage Sites and Landscapes Database' with all documented projects in Africa (and a few Middle East sites e.g. Petra). No India work is mentioned anywhere in independent sources. Treat as 'nothing found, high confidence' rather than a hard-verified negative.

title: Smithsonian Open Access 3D (3d.si.edu) — could not be searched
notes: UNVERIFIED — COULD NOT FETCH. 3d.si.edu is protected by a Cloudflare bot-detection / verification challenge that blocked both the automated web-fetch tool and the browser tool. Per the operating rules for this task, no attempt was made to bypass the CAPTCHA/verification. A site-restricted web search ('site:3d.si.edu Mahabalipuram') returned no matching indexed pages, which is weak evidence of absence but not a substitute for a direct catalog search. RECOMMENDATION: a human should manually check 3d.si.edu's search for 'Mahabalipuram', 'Mamallapuram', 'Shore Temple', and 'Pancha Rathas'.

title: MyMiniFactory 'Scan the World' — no Mahabalipuram content found

title: IGNCA (Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts) digitisation — no Mahabalipuram 3D project found
notes: NOTHING FOUND. Search surfaced only IGNCA's manuscript/document digitisation work (with IHUB Drishti Foundation, IIT Jodhpur) — no mention of 3D scanning of Mahabalipuram or any physical monument. IGNCA's website itself was not directly crawled for a dedicated 3D/photogrammetry archive; this remains a gap a human researcher could close with a direct site search.

title: IIT Madras 'Indian Digital Heritage' project — AI reconstruction of a damaged lion face from Mahabalipuram
source_org: IIT Madras (Prof. A. N. Rajagopalan and Pratyush Sahay), part of DST's Indian Digital Heritage programme
format: Not stated — appears to be a research image/figure, not a distributable 3D asset
captured_by: Pratyush Sahay / A. N. Rajagopalan, IIT Madras
notes: This is an algorithmic/AI 'virtual reconstruction of damaged objects' — i.e. a scan of the current eroded state that is then computationally in-painted/completed to guess the original appearance, shown only as a before/after figure in a student-magazine article about the group's broader Hampi work. NOT a raw measured scan, NOT publicly downloadable, and the specific carving/monument at Mahabalipuram is not identified beyond 'a lion face'. Flagged as a research lead worth a direct inquiry to the lab, not as usable data today.

title: Sea Shore Temple: Reviving Ancient Techniques (La Fondation Dassault Systèmes India + Kural Aram Foundation)
source_org: Kural Aram Foundation (Chennai), supported by La Fondation Dassault Systèmes India
format: Parametric CAD model (Dassault Systèmes tools implied); page mentions potential export to CNC/waterjet/3D-print-ready files, but no public download exists
notes: Page explicitly describes building 'a full parametric 3D model rooted in historical research' of the Shore Temple — this is modeling FROM historical/architectural research, not a direct photogrammetric/LiDAR capture of the standing structure, so it is classified RECONSTRUCTION, not SCAN, despite using professional 3D software. No data download, no license terms, and no confirmation the model even attempts to include the carved figural reliefs (the project appears focused on the temple's parametric/architectural form for craft and fabrication education, e.g. CNC-cutting demonstrations). Worth a direct outreach email but not usable today.

monument: Arjuna's Penance / Descent of the Ganges
title: Wikimedia Commons — Category:Descent of the Ganges (open-licensed photography, including full-panel panoramas)
license: Varies per file; example verified file 'Descent of the Ganges 01.jpg' is dual-licensed CC BY-SA (1.0/2.0/2.5/3.0 Generic) and GFDL 1.2+
format: 2D JPEG photography, NOT a 3D scan or true rectified orthophoto
capture_date: verified file dated 2006-01-29; category holds ~196 files of varying dates
captured_by: Bernard Gagnon (verified file) and numerous other Commons contributors
notes: NOT a scan or orthophoto, but the best openly-licensed 2D reference imagery found for the relief, and the closest thing to a free alternative texture source per the task's own 'orthophoto' fallback path. Category contains several wide/panoramic stitches worth a closer look for the project's UV plate: 'Descent of Ganges panorama.jpg' (6,564 x 1,585 px), 'Arjunas penance Panorama.jpg' (4,531 x 2,161 px), 'Arjuna's penance - 2009.jpg' (7,003 x 2,972 px), 'Mahab Pano1.jpg' (6,108 x 3,550 px) — none of these are true rectified orthophotos (they are perspective photographs/stitches, so straight-on use as a UV texture will show projection distortion), but under CC licenses they are the most legally clean 2D source located. Each file's individual license should be re-checked before use, as Commons categories mix contributors and licenses.
